verdict.rationale: SigNoz's own docs describe service accounts that grant programmatic access to the SigNoz API for CI/CD, automation and external integrations. The dashboard docs also refer to an API path for managing dashboard specs, so a product-provided API clearly exists. However, the pack contains no API reference documentation showing endpoints or coverage, and the OpenAPI probe found no published spec at the standard paths, so how well the API is documented is unproven. The MCP server and Agent Skills belong to separate stories and are not credited here. Missing for 10: published API reference or OpenAPI spec, documented endpoint coverage across signals, alerts and dashboards, and independent hands-on corroboration of driving the product via the API.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Service accounts provide a secure way to grant programmatic API access to SigNoz without tying credentials to individual users.
Use them for CI/CD pipelines, automation scripts, external integrations, and any non-human system that needs to interact with the SigNoz API.
